recent_posts.title: How to show HTML deprecation callouts only when running inside marimo
recent_posts.summary: Components from the wigglystuff library have been promoted into marimo core as of version 0.20.0, including the matrix, pytorch, and chart-select widgets. To handle deprecation gracefully, a helper function detects whether code is running inside marimo (vs. Jupyter) and renders a styled HTML callout with a clickable link instead of a plain Python warning, taking advantage of the fact that marimo always runs in a browser context.

recent_posts.title: all the books in the library
recent_posts.summary: A short reflection drawing on Carl Sagan's quote about the impossibility of reading all books in a library. The author extends this idea to programming languages, tools, frameworks, and LLMs — arguing that the real skill is not consuming everything, but knowing what to ask for or focus on.

recent_posts.title: til uvx deno
recent_posts.summary: You can run Deno, the modern JavaScript/TypeScript runtime, directly from a Python environment using `uvx deno` — no Node.js installation required. This is useful for running simple JavaScript unit tests (e.g., with happy-dom) or as a task runner via `uvx deno task build`, letting Python developers skip the Node toolchain for lightweight JS use cases.

recent_posts.title: til flock
recent_posts.summary: When using cron to auto-deploy with a bash script, concurrent runs can collide if the job takes longer than the cron interval. The `flock` command solves this by acquiring an exclusive file lock before running the script. With the `-n` (non-blocking) flag, any subsequent cron invocation that fires while the lock is held simply exits immediately rather than queuing up. Adding a `timeout` command alongside `flock` also guards against the deploy script hanging indefinitely. This pattern is useful for homelab setups that pull from GitHub on a schedule instead of using webhooks.

recent_posts.title: tailwind shows why mcp might survive
recent_posts.summary: Tailwind CSS had to lay off engineers due to LLMs but is back with ui.sh, a new product that uses an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server to connect AI agents to their service. The author argues this is a smart business model: unlike sharing text files or CLIs, an MCP gives businesses a protected, paywall-able connection point that agents can interact with but can't easily reverse-engineer. This makes MCP a viable path for developer tool businesses to maintain relevance and revenue in an AI-dominated landscape.

recent_posts.title: minimalism as a harness
recent_posts.summary: LLMs generate better code when a language has minimal, unambiguous ways to do things. Python's flexibility works against this, while Lua's simplicity makes it an ideal target for LLM-assisted prototyping. Combined with the LÖVE 2D game engine — which includes APIs for graphics, fonts, sounds, and music generation — it becomes possible to zero-shot a working game prototype with minimal prompting. The author built a clone of the bacteria puzzle from 7th Guest this way, noting the only missing piece was a notebook-style interactive environment for rapid iteration.

recent_posts.title: legos vs 3d printers
recent_posts.summary: A developer reflects on why Python notebooks remain a preferred coding environment, using a lego-vs-3D-printer analogy. Notebooks offer rapid, hands-on iteration — like lego bricks you can swap and recombine — whereas fully vibe-coded apps feel more like 3D-printed objects: flexible to create but hard to modify incrementally. The author argues that interactive, modular coding fosters deeper problem understanding and faster feedback loops.

recent_posts.title: notes on youtube and devrel
recent_posts.summary: Practical tips for DevRel professionals using YouTube as a channel to promote developer tools. Covers thumbnail and title strategy, the importance of storytelling over hooks, short-form vs long-form content tradeoffs, why subscriber counts matter less than watch time, how to avoid being misled by vanity metrics like views, and the value of showing code in action rather than just describing features. Based on experience growing the marimo YouTube channel to 1.5M views and 10K subscribers in one year.

recent_posts.title: prune early and often
recent_posts.summary: uv's caching mechanism can silently consume large amounts of disk space over time, especially when creating many demo projects with isolated environments. Running `uv cache prune` regularly clears stale cache entries — in one instance freeing 168.2GB of disk space.

recent_posts.title: The Sediment of Software Chart
recent_posts.summary: A new open-source project called gitcharts visualizes the evolution of GitHub repositories using 'sediment' charts, which track how lines of code change over time in layers. The charts can overlay version numbers for Python projects, helping correlate code changes with releases. The author suggests these charts can indicate project health — healthy projects show steady code growth without massive rewrites of past code. The project also aims to track the future impact of AI coding agents on codebases.
